finding_dispositions.note: The study-owned defect is cleared in full: the quotation now carries the masculine member of Augustine's sentence and the English states the unus/unum contrast, so no sentence of the study denies the unity of the Incarnation. The clause of required_result asking that research/interpretations.md section 2.3 carry the same clause is the research stage's file and was not done here; the contract forbids this stage revising a reviewed upstream document, and that file is byte-identical to how this dispatch found it.

summary: One blocking finding, STU-016, and it is repaired in the prose this stage owns. The second reading's Alleluia paragraph in sections/30-son-and-lord-of-david.tex quoted only the two neuter members of Augustine's sentence and glossed the first of them as 'the Word and the flesh are not one thing, while the Father and the Word are one', which read plainly denies the unity of the Incarnation, three paragraphs after the same reading says that 'the Word deigned to take our death'. The Latin was read again at the locus in the leaf's own registered tracked text, artifact augustine.enarrationes-in-psalmos.latin-migne-corpus-corporum-wikisource-web-2026-09-05.wikisource-part-11-latin-text, SHA-256 8b9dafef805536c0d4551fc427a6b7060fc1655326b0d1e14507b317dfcf711f recomputed over the tracked file, which holds Migne's Latin of Pss CI-CX and both sermones on Ps 101. Augustine writes at s. 1, 2: 'Jam ergo audiamus quid oret caput et corpus, sponsus et sponsa, Christus et Ecclesia, utrumque unus: sed Verbum et caro non utrumque unum; Pater et Verbum utrumque unum; Christus et Ecclesia utrumque unus, unus quidam vir perfectus in forma plenitudinis suae', then Eph 4:13. The finding's transcription is exact and its reading is right: the antithesis is carried by the gender of the pronoun, three unions set side by side and only the middle one denied. The repair does both of the things the finding admitted rather than one. The quotation is restored to Augustine's own sentence as far as 'unus quidam vir perfectus' -- the masculine member the first reading already quotes at sections/20-whole-heart-one-body.tex -- so the unus/unum contrast is on the page; and the English states it, since English cannot carry it by gender: Christ and the Church are unus, masculine, one man, the perfect man of Eph 4:13; the Father and the Word are unum, neuter, one in substance; the Word and the flesh are not unum in that sense, since Godhead and manhood are not one substance, and they are one person, which is why the head can be called unus with his body in the same breath. The paragraph then says what the distinction is for here: the one Christ is David's son in the flesh he took and David's Lord in the substance he has of the Father. No sentence of the study now states without qualification that the Word and the flesh are not one; the only remaining 'not one' in the nine components is 'not one substance', qualified in its own clause. The locus is unchanged. The finding's required_result also asks that research/interpretations.md section 2.3 carry the clause; that half belongs to the research owner and was not done here, for the reason the leaf's record has given since iteration 5 and the workflow contract states: research/interpretations.md is the research stage's reviewed file and editing it from author-study would be the silent revision of a reviewed upstream document. It is byte-identical to how this dispatch found it, its 2.3 Alleluia row included, and no record of the leaf claims otherwise. STU-006, the standing advisory, is likewise the research owner's and was not touched; it is not reported here. The settled proof is build/claude/liturgy/roman-rite/1962/propers/temporal/57-seventeenth-after-pentecost.pdf, SHA-256 a3309c3634f5fa55fcd632c31819b5870854459c1c31054215a4496c58bde3df, 38 physical pages (inside 20-50), letter, Palatino at 11/15, revision timestamp 2026-09-19T06:20:00Z, which the PDF's own ModDate carries. It settles in two passes, and two independent builds each begun after removing the PDF, log, auxiliary and contents files produced an identical PDF, aux, toc and extracted text, so the proof is a cold fixed point; the log has no error, no LaTeX Warning, no package warning (the fancyhdr headheight warning a wrapped head would raise is absent), no overfull or underfull box, no undefined reference and no rerun request. One heading moves and the extent does not. The repaired paragraph is seven printed lines longer, ten before and seventeen now, so the subsection 'The difficulties this confession must carry' passes the break and stands at page 25 where it stood at page 24; that is the contents file's single changed line, and the auxiliary file's other page assignments are unchanged. Four pages differ in extracted text and only four: pages 23 and 24 carry the repaired paragraph, page 25 receives the heading and the text that already followed it, and page 38 the new timestamp. A cold reviewer holding iteration-6 page numbers should read that one subsection's 'page 24' as page 25. Page 24 now carries 41 body lines where a full page carries 42, because the following subsection could not be set there. Extent: 19,357 words by the same pdftotext -layout measure the iteration-6 record used against that proof's 19,247; a multiset diff accounts for all 110 with nothing over -- 121 tokens added, 11 removed, the removals being the timestamp, the eight words of the replaced gloss, and 'four' and 'senses' leaving a running head as the subsection takes its own head to the next page. Measured as substantive words -- the six argumentative components through Pandoc's LaTeX AST with headings and tables removed -- 13,807 before and 13,918 now, a gain of 111, all in sections/30; with the content of the \latin{} quotations removed, 12,986 and 13,081, a gain of 95. This implementation declares the leaf's own inline commands to Pandoc before converting, because bare Pandoc silently drops the argument of a command it has not been given and so counts no \latin{} or \work{} content at all; that is why the absolute does not reproduce the 13,106 and 12,185 the record carried through iteration 6. The header's figures are restated at the measured numbers and the discontinuity is stated there. All seventeen checks pass at these bytes, with their invocations and output kept beside the proof: check-proper-components (artifacts/research), scripts/_proper_study.py check (content/research, --require-presentation), all twelve check-content-preflight checks the study gate names including provenance-matches-run against this packet's header, check-generation-metadata, check-web-edition, and a trial tools/web-edition conversion, which carries the repaired paragraph through intact, Latin and gloss together. All 38 pages were rendered and both contact sheets read, with pages 23, 24, 25 and 38 inspected individually: no blank page, no heading-only page, no clipping, collision or missing text, every running head a single line. Both companions were rebuilt against the changed shared generation-metadata.tex and build cleanly at their unchanged extents, 12 and 5 pages; they are the derivation stages' to rewrite. Files touched: sections/30-son-and-lord-of-david.tex, generation-metadata.tex (the timestamp and the author-study contribution clause), and research/production-review.md, which records the repair, the proof, the word counts and the two findings left to their research owner. No research evidence was changed and no claim was weakened to make anything pass. The shared-timestamp three-document build and the independent reviews remain the workflow's to obtain.
